summary: Provision cross-functional admin groups, Jira project and Slack channels for new Platform Pod
description: Issue summary: The new Platform Pod (team name: platform-pod) is onboarding and needs a standard set of collaboration artifacts and automations. Impact: Without project/space/channel access and automation, the pod cannot adopt our incident and backlog workflows; oncall handoffs will be manual and slower. Request: 1) Create a Jira project key PLTPOD with default issue types (Bug, Task, Incident) following our internal-support project permission scheme. 2) Provision Confluence space 'Platform Pod' (space key PLTPOD) with view/edit restrictions: Pod members full access; execs and SRE read-only. 3) Create Slack channels: #platform-pod (private, invited: platform-pod-members), #platform-pod-oncall (private, invited: oncall rotation), and public #platform-pod-announcements (posted by integrations only). 4) Create two admin groups in Atlassian: group-platform-pod-admins and group-platform-pod-viewers; populate with initial members listed below. 5) Add automation: a) Jira automation rule that assigns new P0/P1 issues to the current oncall user based on rotation from the oncall calendar. b) Post a webhook to #platform-pod-oncall for all P0 transitions and comment additions with a policy link. c) When a Jira issue is transitioned to 'Incident', create a Confluence incident page using the incident template in the Platform Runbooks space and attach a link in the Jira issue. Acceptance criteria: - PLTPOD Jira project exists and follows permission scheme 'internal-support-standard' - Confluence space created with restrictions and a home page containing the pod charter - Slack channels created with correct privacy and integrations added - Automation rules deployed and tested with a dry-run showing expected behavior - Groups created and initial membership set
request_items: Jira project PLTPOD with permission scheme internal-support-standard
Confluence space PLTPOD with charter and read/edit restrictions
Atlassian groups: group-platform-pod-admins, group-platform-pod-viewers with members
Jira automation: oncall assignment and P0 webhook to Slack
Confluence auto-create from incident transition using incident template
automation_rules: Rule A: On issue created with priority in (P0,P1) assign to current oncall from rota (calendar: /oncall/platform) - dry-run enabled
Rule B: On transition to Incident - create Confluence page from template 'Incident Report' in space PLTPOD and attach link to ticket
Rule C: On priority change to P0 - send webhook payload to Slack channel #platform-pod-oncall with issue summary and link
comments: Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-12: Creating ticket to centralize admin requests for the Platform Pod. Initial members listed; will update membership after confirmation.

Arjun Patel (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Can you confirm whether the announcement channel should allow posting from any member or only integrations? Also confirm SRE read-only access on Confluence is sufficient.
Maya Chen 2026-03-13: Announcement channel should be integrations-only for posts; we will use it for release notes. SRE read-only is fine; platform leads and eng managers should be editors.

Arjun Patel 2026-03-13: Noted. I'll provision the Jira project and groups first, then create the Confluence space. Slack creation requires workspace admin — will trigger approval flow and post here when submitted.
notes: Workaround: Until automation is live, oncall assignments will be manual via the oncall calendar and add @platform-pod-oncall to incidents.
Risk: If automation posts to public announcement channel by mistake, could leak internal P0 info; ensure webhook posts to private oncall channel only.
acceptance_criteria: PLTPOD Jira project created and permission scheme matches internal-support-standard
Confluence space PLTPOD exists, home page set to Pod Charter, editors: platform leads + eng managers
Slack channels created with correct privacy and integration permissions
Automation rules created and tested (dry-run logs attached)
